/wiki/File:Samsung_Galaxy_S4.svgThe Samsung Galaxy S4 from 2013
The Samsung Galaxy S4 was announced by Samsung on March 14, 2013. More than 80 million units of the Galaxy S4 were sold, making it one of the best selling S series phones.[[7]](#cite_note-telegraph_20-7) Some of the highlighted features mostly include the Air Gestures (using the device's proximity and light sensors)[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11)[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) and an IR blaster.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) The Galaxy S4 is one of only two Samsung mobile phones to be equipped with [thermometer](/wiki/Thermometer) and [hygrometer](/wiki/Hygrometer) sensors (the other being the [Galaxy Note 3](/wiki/Galaxy_Note_3)). Some praised the innovation inherent in all of the Galaxy S4's new features,[[16]](#cite_note-16) while others criticized it as [feature creep](/wiki/Feature_creep).[[17]](#cite_note-17)

Other variants of the device are the rugged and water-resistant [S4 Active](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4_Active), the lower-priced mid-class [S4 Mini](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4_Mini), as well as the hybrid [S4 Zoom](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4_Zoom), which is equipped with an [optical zoom](/wiki/Optical_zoom) lens with 10× magnification, more powerful [Xenon flash](/wiki/Xenon_flash), [tripod](/wiki/Tripod) mount, and rotary knob lens ring, combining a mobile phone with a dedicated [digital camera](/wiki/Digital_camera).

/wiki/File:Samsung_Galaxy_S5.pngThe Samsung Galaxy S5 from 2014
The [Samsung Galaxy S5](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S5) was announced on February 24, 2014, offering improvements over its predecessor including a [heart rate](/wiki/Heart_rate) monitor,[[18]](#cite_note-18) IP67 water resistance,[[19]](#cite_note-19) a fingerprint scanner,[[20]](#cite_note-20) 4K video recording,[[21]](#cite_note-21) [phase-detection autofocus](/wiki/Phase-detection_autofocus) plus enhanced low-light photography,[[22]](#cite_note-22) a "Download Booster" feature,[[23]](#cite_note-23) and [USB 3.0](/wiki/USB_3.0).[[24]](#cite_note-24) It lacks the [thermometer](/wiki/Thermometer) (temperature) sensor, [hygrometer](/wiki/Hygrometer) (humidity) sensor, and "Story Album" features from the preceding Galaxy S4, but largely inherited Air View and gesture-related functionality. "Quick glance" was replaced with "Air wake-up", which allows waking up the smartphone from stand-by mode by hovering over the proximity sensor.

The Galaxy S5 is the first Samsung mobile phone where the touch key on the left side of the home button is a task key instead of an option key. It also the last mobile phone in the Galaxy S series with a [micro-SIM](/wiki/Micro-SIM) card (later phones use a [nano-SIM](/wiki/Nano-SIM) card[[25]](#cite_note-4g_sim-25)[[26]](#cite_note-lo_sim-26)) and a user-replaceable battery.

Since the Galaxy S5, the model number (e.g. SM-G900F) is no longer displayed on the boot screen.[[27]](#cite_note-speed-S3-S7-27)

The [Samsung Galaxy S6](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S6) series was first announced on 1 March 2015 with the release of the Galaxy S6 and S6 edge. It marks a counter-utilitarian and fashion-oriented course in the Galaxy S series as it debuted with a new metal and glass build.[[28]](#cite_note-28) The Galaxy S6 series improves upon its predecessors by adding the ability to quickly charge the phone with up to 15W using Qualcomm's [Quick Charge](/wiki/Quick_Charge) 2.0,[[29]](#cite_note-29) virtual reality (compatible with the Galaxy Gear VR), a "Smart Manager" feature,[[30]](#cite_note-30) and the ability to customize the interface with themes.[[31]](#cite_note-31) There were also other variants that were released under the S6 series, which includes the Galaxy S6 Active (first released on 12 June 2015), and the Galaxy S6 edge+ (first released on 13 August 2015, along with the [Galaxy Note5](/wiki/Galaxy_Note5)).

/wiki/File:Samsung_Galaxy_S6_S6_Edge_and_S6_Edge_Plus.pngThe Samsung Galaxy S6 series from 2015
The phone marked its several firsts within the series. It introduced features such as [OIS](/wiki/Image_stabilization), quick launch to open Camera, and a Slow Motion Video Mode. But it is also the first device to remove the [microSD](/wiki/MicroSD) card slot, [Mobile High-Definition Link](/wiki/Mobile_High-Definition_Link) (MHL) support, [water protection](/wiki/IP_Code#Second_digit:_Liquid_ingress_protection), Air Gestures, and [USB 3.0](/wiki/USB_3.0) support. In addition, the batteries in the Galaxy S6 and Galaxy S6 edge are smaller than the battery in the Galaxy S5, and are not replaceable by end users.

Justin Denison, then vice president of product strategy at Samsung, stated on stage at the Unpacked 2015 Episode 1 keynote event that they had opted for a built-in battery now that "consumers could feel confident in charging their phones".[[32]](#cite_note-32)[[33]](#cite_note-33) The previous year, a Samsung commercial for the [Galaxy S5](/wiki/Galaxy_S5) had mocked the [iPhones](/wiki/IPhone)' [non-replaceable batteries](/wiki/Planned_obsolescence#Batteries), referring to iPhone users as "wall huggers", citing their incessant dependence on [wall charging](/wiki/Wall_charger).[[34]](#cite_note-34)

Samsung announced the [Samsung Galaxy S8](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S8) series smartphones on 27 March 2017. They feature an iris scanner, which would be the first of the two S series devices to feature this. S Voice has also been replaced by [Bixby](/wiki/Bixby_(virtual_assistant)). In addition, the [microUSB](/wiki/MicroUSB) port has been replaced by a [USB-C](/wiki/USB-C) 3.0 port, and the physical home button and capacitive buttons have been replaced by on-screen keys. All previous Galaxy S series smartphones featured a 16:9 aspect ratio which was replaced on the Galaxy S8 (18.5:9) for the first time. A new feature called [Samsung DeX](/wiki/Samsung_DeX) was added, allowing the phone to get a desktop user interface when plugged in a monitor. Another variant under this line-up, the Galaxy S8 active, was released on 7 November 2017.

The [Samsung Galaxy S9](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S9) series were unveiled on 25 February 2018 at the [Mobile World Congress](/wiki/Mobile_World_Congress), with an improved camera, redesigned back panel and improved internals. The fingerprint scanner on the back is relocated to below the rear-facing camera, and the earpiece becomes an additional speaker for stereo sound. It is the first flagship phone by Samsung to support recording 2160p (4K) at 60 frames per second (twice as much as the preceding Galaxy S5 to S8), 1080p@240 frames per second (four times as much as the S5 to S8) and super slow motion at 960 frames per second for a limited duration.[[42]](#cite_note-GSMArena-S9-Video-42)[[43]](#cite_note-S9-S8-Note8-43) The first two frame rates are the first increase in the series since the 2014 Samsung Galaxy S5.

Samsung announced the [Galaxy S10](/wiki/Galaxy_S10) series on 20 February 2019 to commemorate the 10th Anniversary of the S Series line-up. It introduced many new features such as an ultrasonic in-display fingerprint scanner, ultra wide lens, reverse wireless charging, 5G and Samsung's first hole-punch selfie camera design. The Galaxy S10 series debuted the [One UI](/wiki/One_UI) software for the first time with [Android 9 Pie](/wiki/Android_9_Pie). The aspect ratio was changed again on the Galaxy S10 series from the Galaxy S8 series, which now features a 19:9 display. For the first time since the Galaxy S5, the series reverts back to using plastic for the back panel which would also later be seen on the A series and the base Galaxy Note that same year. The only exceptions are the Plus models and the S10 5G which still have a glass back panel. The charging rates above 15W supported by the S10 5G and S10 Lite are the first increase on Samsung flagship smartphones since the 2014 [Samsung Galaxy Note 4](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Note_4).[[47]](#cite_note-47)

Samsung announced the [Galaxy S20](/wiki/Galaxy_S20) series on February 11, 2020. On September 23, 2020, the [Galaxy S20 FE](/wiki/Galaxy_S20_FE) was released, a mid-range variant of the S20 containing similar cameras and performance but with less functionality. Another variant is the [Galaxy S20 Tactical Edition](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S20#Samsung_Galaxy_S20_Tactical_Edition), intended for military use. The Galaxy S20 series featured 120 Hz refresh rate displays with 20:9 aspect ratio.

The S20 series are the first Samsung mobile phones with [8K video](/wiki/8K_video) recording (7680×4320p), excluding the S20 FE. Samsung announced the [Galaxy S22](/wiki/Galaxy_S22) series on 9 February 2022. This is the only Galaxy S series lineup (from S20 onwards) to not have a FE version, while its successors have an FE variant (albeit released later than the main devices).

The Galaxy S22 series changed the aspect ratio once again to 19.5:9. The S22 Ultra also upgraded the adaptiveness of the refresh rate from 10–120 Hz to 1–120 Hz.

Both the S22+ and S22 Ultra got upgrades in the charging speed from 25W to 45W. The S22+ and S22 Ultra also got improvements on the display brightness to 1750 nits. Armor Aluminum and [Gorilla Glass](/wiki/Gorilla_Glass) Victus+ also saw an introduction to the S22 series.

/wiki/File:Galaxy_S23.pngThe Samsung Galaxy S23 series from 2023
Samsung announced the [Galaxy S23](/wiki/Galaxy_S23) series on 1 February 2023. In 4 October 2023, the Galaxy S23 FE was released, a mid-range variant of the S23 containing similar cameras and performance but with less functionality. The first three devices would only be equipped with a Qualcomm Snapdragon chipset (on all variants sold globally), a first for the series (all of its predecessors would either have a Samsung Exynos chipset or a Qualcomm Snapdragon chipset, which varies by country).

Like its predecessor, the Galaxy S23 series share the same lineup and screen sizes. The new Galaxy S23 models are equipped with a [Dynamic AMOLED 2X](/wiki/AMOLED) display featuring HDR10+ support, dynamic tone mapping technology, and a peak brightness of 1750 nits. The S23 supports USB-C wired charging at up to 25W using USB Power Delivery, while the S23+ and S23 Ultra offer faster 45W charging. All three models feature [Qi inductive charging](/wiki/Qi_(standard)) up to 15W and Wireless PowerShare, which enables the phones to charge other Qi-compatible devices from their own batteries at up to 4.5W. The phones are launched with [Android 13](/wiki/Android_13) and Samsung's [One UI 5.1](/wiki/One_UI) software.

/wiki/File:Samsung_Galaxy_S4.svgThe Samsung Galaxy S4 from 2013
The Samsung Galaxy S4 was announced by Samsung on March 14, 2013. More than 80 million units of the Galaxy S4 were sold, making it one of the best selling S series phones.[[7]](#cite_note-telegraph_20-7) Some of the highlighted features mostly include the Air Gestures (using the device's proximity and light sensors)[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11)[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) and an IR blaster.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) The Galaxy S4 is one of only two Samsung mobile phones to be equipped with [thermometer](/wiki/Thermometer) and [hygrometer](/wiki/Hygrometer) sensors (the other being the [Galaxy Note 3](/wiki/Galaxy_Note_3)). Some praised the innovation inherent in all of the Galaxy S4's new features,[[16]](#cite_note-16) while others criticized it as [feature creep](/wiki/Feature_creep).[[17]](#cite_note-17)

Other variants of the device are the rugged and water-resistant [S4 Active](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4_Active), the lower-priced mid-class [S4 Mini](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4_Mini), as well as the hybrid [S4 Zoom](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4_Zoom), which is equipped with an [optical zoom](/wiki/Optical_zoom) lens with 10× magnification, more powerful [Xenon flash](/wiki/Xenon_flash), [tripod](/wiki/Tripod) mount, and rotary knob lens ring, combining a mobile phone with a dedicated [digital camera](/wiki/Digital_camera).

The [Samsung Galaxy S5](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S5) was announced on February 24, 2014, offering improvements over its predecessor including a [heart rate](/wiki/Heart_rate) monitor,[[18]](#cite_note-18) IP67 water resistance,[[19]](#cite_note-19) a fingerprint scanner,[[20]](#cite_note-20) 4K video recording,[[21]](#cite_note-21) [phase-detection autofocus](/wiki/Phase-detection_autofocus) plus enhanced low-light photography,[[22]](#cite_note-22) a "Download Booster" feature,[[23]](#cite_note-23) and [USB 3.0](/wiki/USB_3.0).[[24]](#cite_note-24) It lacks the [thermometer](/wiki/Thermometer) (temperature) sensor, [hygrometer](/wiki/Hygrometer) (humidity) sensor, and "Story Album" features from the preceding Galaxy S4, but largely inherited Air View and gesture-related functionality. "Quick glance" was replaced with "Air wake-up", which allows waking up the smartphone from stand-by mode by hovering over the proximity sensor.

The Galaxy S5 is the first Samsung mobile phone where the touch key on the left side of the home button is a task key instead of an option key. It also the last mobile phone in the Galaxy S series with a [micro-SIM](/wiki/Micro-SIM) card (later phones use a [nano-SIM](/wiki/Nano-SIM) card[[25]](#cite_note-4g_sim-25)[[26]](#cite_note-lo_sim-26)) and a user-replaceable battery.

Since the Galaxy S5, the model number (e.g. SM-G900F) is no longer displayed on the boot screen.[[27]](#cite_note-speed-S3-S7-27)

The [Samsung Galaxy S6](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S6) series was first announced on 1 March 2015 with the release of the Galaxy S6 and S6 edge. It marks a counter-utilitarian and fashion-oriented course in the Galaxy S series as it debuted with a new metal and glass build.[[28]](#cite_note-28) The Galaxy S6 series improves upon its predecessors by adding the ability to quickly charge the phone with up to 15W using Qualcomm's [Quick Charge](/wiki/Quick_Charge) 2.0,[[29]](#cite_note-29) virtual reality (compatible with the Galaxy Gear VR), a "Smart Manager" feature,[[30]](#cite_note-30) and the ability to customize the interface with themes.[[31]](#cite_note-31) There were also other variants that were released under the S6 series, which includes the Galaxy S6 Active (first released on 12 June 2015), and the Galaxy S6 edge+ (first released on 13 August 2015, along with the [Galaxy Note5](/wiki/Galaxy_Note5)).

/wiki/File:Samsung_Galaxy_S6_S6_Edge_and_S6_Edge_Plus.pngThe Samsung Galaxy S6 series from 2015
The phone marked its several firsts within the series. It introduced features such as [OIS](/wiki/Image_stabilization), quick launch to open Camera, and a Slow Motion Video Mode. But it is also the first device to remove the [microSD](/wiki/MicroSD) card slot, [Mobile High-Definition Link](/wiki/Mobile_High-Definition_Link) (MHL) support, [water protection](/wiki/IP_Code#Second_digit:_Liquid_ingress_protection), Air Gestures, and [USB 3.0](/wiki/USB_3.0) support. In addition, the batteries in the Galaxy S6 and Galaxy S6 edge are smaller than the battery in the Galaxy S5, and are not replaceable by end users.

Justin Denison, then vice president of product strategy at Samsung, stated on stage at the Unpacked 2015 Episode 1 keynote event that they had opted for a built-in battery now that "consumers could feel confident in charging their phones".[[32]](#cite_note-32)[[33]](#cite_note-33) The previous year, a Samsung commercial for the [Galaxy S5](/wiki/Galaxy_S5) had mocked the [iPhones](/wiki/IPhone)' [non-replaceable batteries](/wiki/Planned_obsolescence#Batteries), referring to iPhone users as "wall huggers", citing their incessant dependence on [wall charging](/wiki/Wall_charger).[[34]](#cite_note-34)

The S21 series also drops [MST](/wiki/Magnetic_secure_transmission) technology previously used for [Samsung Pay](/wiki/Samsung_Pay) which gave Galaxy phones the ability to pay without needing [NFC](/wiki/Near-field_communication).

Samsung announced the [Galaxy S23](/wiki/Galaxy_S23) series on 1 February 2023. In 4 October 2023, the Galaxy S23 FE was released, a mid-range variant of the S23 containing similar cameras and performance but with less functionality. All three models feature [Qi inductive charging](/wiki/Qi_(standard)) up to 15W and Wireless PowerShare, which enables the phones to charge other Qi-compatible devices from their own batteries at up to 4.5W. The phones are launched with [Android 13](/wiki/Android_13) and Samsung's [One UI 5.1](/wiki/One_UI) software.

The Samsung Galaxy Note series is a discontinued line of high-end flagship [Android](/wiki/Android_(operating_system)) [phablets](/wiki/Phablet) manufactured, developed and marketed by [Samsung Electronics](/wiki/Samsung_Electronics). The line was primarily oriented towards [pen computing](/wiki/Pen_computing); all Galaxy Note models shipped with a [stylus pen](/wiki/Stylus_(computing)), called the [S Pen](/wiki/S_Pen), and incorporate a pressure-sensitive [Wacom](/wiki/Wacom_(company)) [digitizer](/wiki/Graphics_tablet). All Galaxy Note models also include software features that are oriented towards the stylus and the devices' large screens, such as [note-taking](/wiki/Note-taking), [digital scrapbooking](/wiki/Digital_scrapbooking) apps, [tooltips](/wiki/Tooltip), and split-screen multitasking. The line served as [Samsung](/wiki/Samsung)'s flagship smartphone model, positioned and slotted above the [Galaxy S series](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S_series), and was part of the wider [Samsung Galaxy](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy) series of Android computing devices.

The Galaxy Note smartphone series is noteworthy for being considered the first commercially successful examples of "[phablets](/wiki/Phablet)"—a class of smartphones with large screens that are intended to straddle the functionality of a traditional tablet with that of a phone, and having helped accelerate the trend of bigger screened smartphones becoming the norm around the mid 2010s. Samsung sold over 50 million Galaxy Note devices between September 2011 and October 2013.

In August 2021, TM Roh, Samsung's president and head of mobile communications, announced that no new Galaxy Note device would be unveiled at their 2021 launch event, which would instead focus on new foldable phones. "Instead of unveiling a new Galaxy Note this time around, we will further broaden beloved Note features to more Samsung Galaxy devices," he added.[[1]](#cite_note-1) Phablet-sized Galaxy products are still being produced as "Ultra" editions of certain models in the [Galaxy S series](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S_series) since the [Galaxy S22](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S22).[[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]

Samsung announced the original Galaxy Note at [IFA Berlin](/wiki/IFA_Berlin) in 2011. While some media outlets questioned the viability of the device due to its 5.3-inch (130 mm) screen (which, at the time, was considered extremely large for a phone), the Note received positive reception for its stylus functionality, the speed of its 1.4 GHz dual-core processor, and the advantages of such a large screen size. Like the Galaxy S2 from earlier that year, the camera has eight megapixels and can film in Full HD, 1080p, and the device features [Mobile High-Definition Link](/wiki/Mobile_High-Definition_Link) (MHL to [HDMI](/wiki/HDMI)).[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-techradar-originalgn-3)

The Galaxy Note is a commercial success: released in October 2011, [Samsung](/wiki/Samsung) announced in September 2011, that the [Galaxy](/wiki/Galaxy) Note had sold 1 million units in two months. In February 2012, Samsung debuted a Note version with [LTE](/wiki/LTE_(telecommunication)) support, and by August 2012, the Note had sold 10 million units worldwide.[[4]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

On 29 August 2012, at IFA Berlin, Samsung unveiled a successor to the Galaxy Note, the Galaxy Note II. The new model, released September 2012, featured improvements to the original Note's hardware (with a quad-core processor and a larger 51⁄2-inch (140 mm) display, a revised stylus that can reveal [Air View](/wiki/Air_View) tooltips through hovering, and an upgraded digitizer with 1,024 levels of pressure sensitivity for more precise pen input, a new hardware design based on that of the [Galaxy S III](/wiki/Galaxy_S_III)), along with new features such as pen gestures, split-screen multitasking, Air View (which allows previews of content to be displayed by hovering the pen above the screen), and other new features also introduced by the S III.[[6]](#cite_note-note2review-engadget-6)

On 4 September 2013, Samsung unveiled the Galaxy Note 3, which introduced a more "premium" design with a [plastic leather](/wiki/Plastic_leather) backing, and a 5.7-inch (145 mm) [1080p](/wiki/1080p) display, 3 GB of [RAM](/wiki/Random_access_memory), new [4K](/wiki/4K_resolution) video recording capabilities at 30 frames per second (up to 5 minutes per video; availability varies per region), [1080p](/wiki/1080p) at twice the framerate (60fps "smooth motion" option), a [USB 3.0](/wiki/USB_3.0) connector, an [infrared](/wiki/Infrared) transmitter for use as [remote control](/wiki/Remote_control), a third microphone for noise cancellation, [multi-windowing](/wiki/Window_(computing)), and expanded stylus pen functionality.[[7]](#cite_note-cnet-gn3handson-7)[[8]](#cite_note-verge-usb3-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) Unlike its predecessor, it is not equipped with an [FM radio](/wiki/FM_radio). The speaker is placed at the bottom,[[10]](#cite_note-N3pics-10) while placed on the rear side on the Note 1, 2 and 4.

The Note 3 is the only Galaxy Note device to be equipped with [thermometer](/wiki/Thermometer) and [hygrometer](/wiki/Hygrometer) sensors and [Air View](/wiki/Air_View) support for both stylus and fingers, of which the latter is achieved with an additional [self-capacitive](/wiki/Touchscreen#Self-capacitance)[[11]](#cite_note-SonyDev-11) [touch screen](/wiki/Touch_screen) layer. It also had additional voice commands, including "Dismiss" and "Snooze" for the alarm, and "Answer" and "Decline" for calls.

In January 2014, Samsung for the first time released a "downgraded" version of the Note 3, the Galaxy Note 3 Neo. It features the S-Pen stylus, 8 MP camera, 5.5" Super AMOLED HD 720p display, 16 GB storage, 2 GB RAM as well as some of the Note 3's software features (e.g. screen zoom).

For the first time, it has a Samsung Exynos Hexa 5260 (6 core) processor with a quad-core 1.3 GHz Cortex A7 CPU and a dual-core 1.7 GHz Cortex A15 CPU with support for HMP and a Mali-T624 GPU.

The Note 3 Neo lacks both 4K (2160p) and [slow motion](/wiki/Slow_motion) (720p@120fps) video recording and can record 1080p at only up to 30 frames per second.

On 3 September 2014, at IFA Berlin, Samsung unveiled a successor to the Galaxy Note 3, the Galaxy Note 4. The new model, released on 3 September 2014, introduced a new design with a [plastic leather](/wiki/Plastic_leather) backing and metal frame, a 5.7-inch (145 mm) QHD display, a 16 MP camera with then new [optical image stabilization](/wiki/Optical_image_stabilization), 15 watts of fast charging using [Qualcomm Quick Charge](/wiki/Qualcomm_Quick_Charge) 2.0, revised multi-windowing,[[12]](#cite_note-12) an improved S-Pen stylus, an upgraded digitizer with 2,048 levels of pressure sensitivity and expanded functionality, fingerprint scanner, and other features taken from the [Galaxy S5](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S5). However, Samsung [Air View](/wiki/Air_View) is only usable with the S-Pen, while it was usable with both fingers and stylus on the Galaxy Note 3.

The Galaxy Note 4 is uniquely equipped with an [ultraviolet](/wiki/Ultraviolet) ray sensor, and the last Samsung flagship phone to be equipped with a user-replaceable battery.[[13]](#cite_note-GSMarena-Note4-13)

Alongside the Galaxy Note 4, Samsung also unveiled the Galaxy Note Edge, which features a display with a curved portion that wraps around the right [bezel](/wiki/Bezel_(screen)) of the device. The curved area can be used as a sidebar to display news and information tickers, application shortcuts, and other tools.[[14]](#cite_note-cnet-noteedgecomfort-14)[[15]](#cite_note-gsmarena-review-15)

The curved right side screen area extends the resolution of the display from 1440×2560 to 1600×2560.

The Galaxy Note 4 and Galaxy Note Edge are the last in the Note series to use [micro-SIM](/wiki/Micro-SIM) cards. Later models in the series use [nano-SIM](/wiki/Nano-SIM) cards.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

The Galaxy Note 5 was announced on 13 August 2015. It is based upon the specifications, hardware and exterior design of the [Galaxy S6](/wiki/Galaxy_S6), including its metal frame and glass backing, but with a larger 5.7-inch 1440p display, [Exynos](/wiki/Exynos) 7 Octa 7420 [system-on-chip](/wiki/System-on-chip), as well as a new spring-loaded stylus slot. As with the S6 and unlike previous Note models, the Note 5 does not offer a user-replaceable battery or expandable storage. Other removed features include support for Mobile High-Definition Link, a third microphone, and an infrared transmitter.[[17]](#cite_note-techradar-5review-17)[[18]](#cite_note-engadget-slotbreakstylusfix-18)[[19]](#cite_note-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20) The new "Screen off memo" feature allows the phone to be awoken directly to a note screen when the stylus is removed,[[17]](#cite_note-techradar-5review-17) and the camera app allows public and private [livestreaming](/wiki/Livestreaming) directly to YouTube.[[17]](#cite_note-techradar-5review-17)

The Galaxy Note 7 was announced during a press event in New York City on 2 August 2016. It is largely based on the hardware of the [Galaxy S7](/wiki/Galaxy_S7), inheriting its processor, camera, and the restoration of [IP68](/wiki/IP68) water resistance and expandable storage, but with a larger 5.7-inch 1440p display. It is also Samsung's first device to feature a [USB-C](/wiki/USB-C) connector and the first water-protected device of the [Galaxy Note series](/wiki/Galaxy_Note_series), having a water-protected stylus too.

The Galaxy Note 7's display is curved across the sides of the device, and its stylus features higher degrees of pressure sensitivity (4096) and a finer tip.[[21]](#cite_note-verge-s7unveil-21)[[22]](#cite_note-ars-note7unveil-22) Samsung branded the device as the Note 7 rather than the Note 6 to synchronize its branding with the earlier flagship of the same year, the [Samsung Galaxy S7 series](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S7).[[23]](#cite_note-verge-gn7-23)

Upon release, the Galaxy Note series earned [criticism by a technology journalist of Android Police](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Note_7#Android_Police), criticizing that since 2015's Galaxy Note 5, not much except a stylus sets the Galaxy Note series flagship apart from the [Galaxy S series](/wiki/Galaxy_S_series) flagship released earlier in the same year, like it did with the first four generations of Galaxy Note devices.[[24]](#cite_note-AndroidPolice-24)

The Galaxy Note 7 was afflicted by repeated manufacturing problems with their internal batteries, which led to incidents in which they overheated and combusted.[[25]](#cite_note-verge-cause-25)[[26]](#cite_note-recode-cause-26) After replacement models experienced similar incidents, the Note 7 was officially discontinued on 11 October 2016, and nearly all units were recalled globally.[[27]](#cite_note-verge-note7isdead-27)[[28]](#cite_note-bbc-gn7done-28)

#### Galaxy Note Fan Edition
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=10)]

After the recall of the Samsung Galaxy Note 7, Samsung released the Note Fan Edition (FE) as a [refurbished](/wiki/Refurbishment_(electronics)) Note 7 in selected countries on 7 July 2017. Although having an identical form factor, the Fan Edition comes with a smaller battery of only 3200 mAh rather than the original Note 7 which is 3500 mAh due to safety reasons.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

Improved changes of the Galaxy Note Fan Edition include [Android Nougat](/wiki/Android_Nougat) with [Samsung Experience](/wiki/Samsung_Experience) 8.1 UI, [Bixby](/wiki/Bixby_(virtual_assistant)) virtual assistant (excluding Voice), a "Fan Edition" marking on the back and a Clear View Cover case.

The Samsung Galaxy Note 8 was announced on 23 August 2017. It features a 6.3" [1440p](/wiki/1440p) [Super AMOLED](/wiki/Super_AMOLED) Infinity Display, a 3300 mAh battery, Qualcomm [Quick Charge](/wiki/Quick_Charge) 2.0 support, [Snapdragon](/wiki/Qualcomm_Snapdragon) [835](/wiki/List_of_Snapdragon_devices#Snapdragon_835)/[Exynos](/wiki/Exynos) 8895 processor (depending on location), an [iris scanner](/wiki/Iris_scanner), IP68 dust and water resistance, a new dual-lens camera setup with a [telephoto lens](/wiki/Telephoto_lens) and support for [Samsung DeX](/wiki/Samsung_DeX).
[[30]](#cite_note-30)

On 27 June 2018, Samsung sent out invitations for the next "Unpacked" event, showing a yellow S Pen image. The Galaxy Note 9 was subsequently announced on 9 August 2018 and became available starting on 24 August 2018.[[31]](#cite_note-31)[[32]](#cite_note-32)

The Note 9 is a largely refined version of the Note 8. The biggest change from the Note 8 was the addition of [Bluetooth](/wiki/Bluetooth) functionality to the S-Pen, allowing a user to control the camera, YouTube videos and slideshows remotely.[[33]](#cite_note-33)

Internally, the Note 9 uses the [Snapdragon](/wiki/List_of_Qualcomm_Snapdragon_systems-on-chip) 845 or Exynos 9810 processor, with either 6 GB of RAM and 128 GB of internal storage, or 8 GB of RAM and 512 GB of internal storage, and a 4000 mAh battery.[[34]](#cite_note-34)

The Note 9 uses the same camera hardware seen on [Samsung Galaxy S9](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S9) Plus, with a dual camera setup, a 12MP wide-angle sensor with f/1.5 and f/2.4 dual aperture and a 12MP telephoto sensor with the f/2.4 aperture for [Bokeh](/wiki/Bokeh) effects at the back, along with an 8MP selfie camera.[[35]](#cite_note-35)

### Galaxy Note 10/Note 10+
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=13)]

On 1 July 2019, Samsung announced that it would hold its second Unpacked event of the year on 7 August at 16:00 Eastern in Brooklyn's Barclays Center. The Galaxy Note 10 and Note 10+ were unveiled at the show.[[36]](#cite_note-36)[[37]](#cite_note-37)

The Note 10 marked the first time Samsung offered a Plus model of its Note, with the Note 10 offering a 6.3-inch 1080p display Infinity-O Display and 3400 mAh battery, and the Note 10+ offering a 6.8-inch 1440p display with a 4300 mAh battery. The Note 10 has non-expandable 256 GB storage, while the Note 10+ has expandable 256/512 GB storage via microSD. Both phones added several new features from the [Samsung Galaxy S10](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S10), including in-display fingerprint scanners, Wireless Powershare (enabling the phone to be used to wirelessly charge other Qi-compatible devices), and triple camera arrays consisting of a 16MP ultra-wide angle lens and 12MP wide angle and telephoto lenses. Both variants also saw the power button consolidated with the Bixby button on the left side of the phone, with the button now being reprogrammable to be used as a power button or to activate Bixby, and eliminated the headphone jack.

Also introduced with the Note 10 variants were 25 watts Super Fast Charging (with the Note 10+ also being capable of 45 watt Super Fast Charging 2.0), marking the first charging rate increase since the 2014 Galaxy Note 4.[[38]](#cite_note-38)[[39]](#cite_note-verge-s10unveil-39)

#### Galaxy Note 10 Lite
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=14)]

On 3 January 2020, Samsung announced alongside the Galaxy S10 Lite, the upcoming release of the Note 10 Lite.[[40]](#cite_note-40) The Note 10 Lite's main points of interest were that it reintroduced design elements and features had not been used the flagship Note devices in a few generations, such as an entirely flat display (last seen on the Note 5), the reintroduction of the headphone jack (last seen on the Note 9), and the inclusion of an FM radio. Internally, the Note 10 Lite had the older chipset, processor, and GPU from the Exynos version of the Note 9, while incorporating newer features such as the triple cameras seen in the rest of the Note 10 series. To position itself, much as the Note 3 Neo had done, as a more affordable Note device, the pricing was much more comparable to midrange handsets of the time at under half the price of the Note 10+ and lesser than the Note 10. It had introduced the spen to the public at an affordable cost.

### Galaxy Note 20/Note 20 Ultra
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=15)]

Samsung announced the Galaxy Note 20 and Note 20 Ultra at a virtual Unpacked Event on 5 August 2020. Both came in variants with and without [5G](/wiki/5G) connectivity.

Like the Note 10 line, Note 20 has lesser specifications to justify a relatively lower price point, while the Note 20 Ultra is positioned as a high-end premium device. In this case, the Note 20 Ultra has a 6.9-inch display, 120 Hz refresh rate, 4,500 mAh battery, and expandable storage. The Note 20 lacks several key features of the Note 20 Ultra, including the high [refresh rate](/wiki/Refresh_rate), [microSD](/wiki/MicroSD) storage expansion and "periscope" [zoom lens](/wiki/Zoom_lens). Both phones have triple camera setups similar to the S20 line, with the Note 20 using two 12 MP wide and ultrawide sensors and a 64 MP telephoto sensor, and the Note 20 Ultra using a 108 MP wide sensor and two 12 MP telephoto and ultrawide sensors.[[41]](#cite_note-GSMArena-comparison-41) On both models, the buttons and S-Pen have switched places from their positions on the Note 10, with the power and volume buttons now being on the right side of the phone, and the S-Pen dock now moved to the left side of the USB-C port.

This is the last phone launched under the Note series, before Samsung decided to add support for S-Pen in the Galaxy S series and Z Fold series, beginning with the [Galaxy S21 Ultra](/wiki/Galaxy_S21_Ultra) and [Galaxy Z Fold 3](/wiki/Galaxy_Z_Fold_3). The [Galaxy S22 Ultra](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S22), launched in February 2022, features a built-in S-Pen.

The Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 is an 8-inch Android-based tablet computer produced and marketed by Samsung Electronics. It belongs to the second generation of the Samsung Galaxy Note series tablets, which also includes a 10.1-inch model, the Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition.

At the [Mobile World Congress](/wiki/Mobile_World_Congress) 2012, Samsung announced the Galaxy Note 10.1, as an alternative to the Galaxy Tab 10.1. It has a 10.1-inch display and uses a quad-core 1.4 GHz processor and supports the Samsung S-Pen stylus input as seen on the original Galaxy Note phone.

### Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=19)]

At the 2013 Samsung Unpacked Episode 2 event in Berlin and New York, Samsung announced the successor to the original Galaxy Note 10.1-inch tablet dubbed as the Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition. Like its predecessor, it has a 10.1 inch display and now supports the improved Samsung S-Pen stylus input also seen in the Note III and it copies the design cue of its lower-end sibling the [Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Tab_3_10.1) which sports the unified Samsung design first used on the [Samsung Galaxy S4](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4).

### Galaxy Note Pro 12.2
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=20)]

At the 2014 Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Samsung announced the first Pro line of tablets which included a bigger Samsung Galaxy Note Pro tablet with a 12.2-inch display and also comes with the same S-Pen stylus the [Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Note_10.1_2014_Edition) is sporting which is the standard on the Note Series. Its design is similar to the [Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Note_10.1_2014_Edition) which has the Samsung standard simulated stitched-leather back.

Subsequently, released together with the first regular Tab A 8.0 and 9.7 models in 2015, Samsung released a model of the Tab A 9.7 equipped with an S-Pen stylus making it the first Samsung Galaxy device to be equipped with the Samsung stylus outside the Note series. In 2017 Samsung released another S-Pen device, the Tab S3. On 1 August 2018, Samsung launched the new tablet: Samsung Galaxy Tab S4 with a new S-Pen. Subsequently, in 2019, Samsung launched the Galaxy Tab S6 with the S-Pen.

The Galaxy S21 Ultra was announced at the Galaxy Unpacked event on 14 January 2021, alongside the Galaxy S21 and Galaxy S21+. The Galaxy S21 Ultra is the first phone in the Galaxy S Series to support the S Pen accessory, albeit sold separately and with limited functionality. It features a 6.8" 1440p "Dynamic AMOLED" curved display with HDR10+ support, "dynamic tone mapping" technology, and a variable 120 Hz [refresh rate](/wiki/Refresh_rate).

The Galaxy S22 Ultra was announced at the Galaxy Unpacked event on 9 February 2022, alongside the Galaxy S22 and Galaxy S22+. Unlike the Galaxy S21 Ultra, the Galaxy S22 features an embedded S Pen, with similar functionalities to the Galaxy Note series and with a faster pen latency of 2.8ms.

The Samsung Galaxy Note series is a discontinued line of high-end flagship [Android](/wiki/Android_(operating_system)) [phablets](/wiki/Phablet) manufactured, developed and marketed by [Samsung Electronics](/wiki/Samsung_Electronics). The line was primarily oriented towards [pen computing](/wiki/Pen_computing); all Galaxy Note models shipped with a [stylus pen](/wiki/Stylus_(computing)), called the [S Pen](/wiki/S_Pen), and incorporate a pressure-sensitive [Wacom](/wiki/Wacom_(company)) [digitizer](/wiki/Graphics_tablet). All Galaxy Note models also include software features that are oriented towards the stylus and the devices' large screens, such as [note-taking](/wiki/Note-taking), [digital scrapbooking](/wiki/Digital_scrapbooking) apps, [tooltips](/wiki/Tooltip), and split-screen multitasking. The line served as [Samsung](/wiki/Samsung)'s flagship smartphone model, positioned and slotted above the [Galaxy S series](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S_series), and was part of the wider [Samsung Galaxy](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy) series of Android computing devices.

The Galaxy Note smartphone series is noteworthy for being considered the first commercially successful examples of "[phablets](/wiki/Phablet)"—a class of smartphones with large screens that are intended to straddle the functionality of a traditional tablet with that of a phone, and having helped accelerate the trend of bigger screened smartphones becoming the norm around the mid 2010s. Samsung sold over 50 million Galaxy Note devices between September 2011 and October 2013.

In August 2021, TM Roh, Samsung's president and head of mobile communications, announced that no new Galaxy Note device would be unveiled at their 2021 launch event, which would instead focus on new foldable phones. "Instead of unveiling a new Galaxy Note this time around, we will further broaden beloved Note features to more Samsung Galaxy devices," he added.[[1]](#cite_note-1) Phablet-sized Galaxy products are still being produced as "Ultra" editions of certain models in the [Galaxy S series](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S_series) since the [Galaxy S22](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S22).[[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]

Samsung announced the original Galaxy Note at [IFA Berlin](/wiki/IFA_Berlin) in 2011. While some media outlets questioned the viability of the device due to its 5.3-inch (130 mm) screen (which, at the time, was considered extremely large for a phone), the Note received positive reception for its stylus functionality, the speed of its 1.4 GHz dual-core processor, and the advantages of such a large screen size. Like the Galaxy S2 from earlier that year, the camera has eight megapixels and can film in Full HD, 1080p, and the device features [Mobile High-Definition Link](/wiki/Mobile_High-Definition_Link) (MHL to [HDMI](/wiki/HDMI)).[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-techradar-originalgn-3)

The Galaxy Note is a commercial success: released in October 2011, [Samsung](/wiki/Samsung) announced in September 2011, that the [Galaxy](/wiki/Galaxy) Note had sold 1 million units in two months. In February 2012, Samsung debuted a Note version with [LTE](/wiki/LTE_(telecommunication)) support, and by August 2012, the Note had sold 10 million units worldwide.[[4]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

On 29 August 2012, at IFA Berlin, Samsung unveiled a successor to the Galaxy Note, the Galaxy Note II. The new model, released September 2012, featured improvements to the original Note's hardware (with a quad-core processor and a larger 51⁄2-inch (140 mm) display, a revised stylus that can reveal [Air View](/wiki/Air_View) tooltips through hovering, and an upgraded digitizer with 1,024 levels of pressure sensitivity for more precise pen input, a new hardware design based on that of the [Galaxy S III](/wiki/Galaxy_S_III)), along with new features such as pen gestures, split-screen multitasking, Air View (which allows previews of content to be displayed by hovering the pen above the screen), and other new features also introduced by the S III.[[6]](#cite_note-note2review-engadget-6)

On 4 September 2013, Samsung unveiled the Galaxy Note 3, which introduced a more "premium" design with a [plastic leather](/wiki/Plastic_leather) backing, and a 5.7-inch (145 mm) [1080p](/wiki/1080p) display, 3 GB of [RAM](/wiki/Random_access_memory), new [4K](/wiki/4K_resolution) video recording capabilities at 30 frames per second (up to 5 minutes per video; availability varies per region), [1080p](/wiki/1080p) at twice the framerate (60fps "smooth motion" option), a [USB 3.0](/wiki/USB_3.0) connector, an [infrared](/wiki/Infrared) transmitter for use as [remote control](/wiki/Remote_control), a third microphone for noise cancellation, [multi-windowing](/wiki/Window_(computing)), and expanded stylus pen functionality.[[7]](#cite_note-cnet-gn3handson-7)[[8]](#cite_note-verge-usb3-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) Unlike its predecessor, it is not equipped with an [FM radio](/wiki/FM_radio). The speaker is placed at the bottom,[[10]](#cite_note-N3pics-10) while placed on the rear side on the Note 1, 2 and 4.

The Note 3 is the only Galaxy Note device to be equipped with [thermometer](/wiki/Thermometer) and [hygrometer](/wiki/Hygrometer) sensors and [Air View](/wiki/Air_View) support for both stylus and fingers, of which the latter is achieved with an additional [self-capacitive](/wiki/Touchscreen#Self-capacitance)[[11]](#cite_note-SonyDev-11) [touch screen](/wiki/Touch_screen) layer. It also had additional voice commands, including "Dismiss" and "Snooze" for the alarm, and "Answer" and "Decline" for calls.

In January 2014, Samsung for the first time released a "downgraded" version of the Note 3, the Galaxy Note 3 Neo. It features the S-Pen stylus, 8 MP camera, 5.5" Super AMOLED HD 720p display, 16 GB storage, 2 GB RAM as well as some of the Note 3's software features (e.g. screen zoom).

For the first time, it has a Samsung Exynos Hexa 5260 (6 core) processor with a quad-core 1.3 GHz Cortex A7 CPU and a dual-core 1.7 GHz Cortex A15 CPU with support for HMP and a Mali-T624 GPU.

The Note 3 Neo lacks both 4K (2160p) and [slow motion](/wiki/Slow_motion) (720p@120fps) video recording and can record 1080p at only up to 30 frames per second.

On 3 September 2014, at IFA Berlin, Samsung unveiled a successor to the Galaxy Note 3, the Galaxy Note 4. The new model, released on 3 September 2014, introduced a new design with a [plastic leather](/wiki/Plastic_leather) backing and metal frame, a 5.7-inch (145 mm) QHD display, a 16 MP camera with then new [optical image stabilization](/wiki/Optical_image_stabilization), 15 watts of fast charging using [Qualcomm Quick Charge](/wiki/Qualcomm_Quick_Charge) 2.0, revised multi-windowing,[[12]](#cite_note-12) an improved S-Pen stylus, an upgraded digitizer with 2,048 levels of pressure sensitivity and expanded functionality, fingerprint scanner, and other features taken from the [Galaxy S5](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S5). However, Samsung [Air View](/wiki/Air_View) is only usable with the S-Pen, while it was usable with both fingers and stylus on the Galaxy Note 3.

The Galaxy Note 4 is uniquely equipped with an [ultraviolet](/wiki/Ultraviolet) ray sensor, and the last Samsung flagship phone to be equipped with a user-replaceable battery.[[13]](#cite_note-GSMarena-Note4-13)

Alongside the Galaxy Note 4, Samsung also unveiled the Galaxy Note Edge, which features a display with a curved portion that wraps around the right [bezel](/wiki/Bezel_(screen)) of the device. The curved area can be used as a sidebar to display news and information tickers, application shortcuts, and other tools.[[14]](#cite_note-cnet-noteedgecomfort-14)[[15]](#cite_note-gsmarena-review-15)

The curved right side screen area extends the resolution of the display from 1440×2560 to 1600×2560.

The Galaxy Note 4 and Galaxy Note Edge are the last in the Note series to use [micro-SIM](/wiki/Micro-SIM) cards. Later models in the series use [nano-SIM](/wiki/Nano-SIM) cards.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

The Galaxy Note 5 was announced on 13 August 2015. It is based upon the specifications, hardware and exterior design of the [Galaxy S6](/wiki/Galaxy_S6), including its metal frame and glass backing, but with a larger 5.7-inch 1440p display, [Exynos](/wiki/Exynos) 7 Octa 7420 [system-on-chip](/wiki/System-on-chip), as well as a new spring-loaded stylus slot. As with the S6 and unlike previous Note models, the Note 5 does not offer a user-replaceable battery or expandable storage. Other removed features include support for Mobile High-Definition Link, a third microphone, and an infrared transmitter.[[17]](#cite_note-techradar-5review-17)[[18]](#cite_note-engadget-slotbreakstylusfix-18)[[19]](#cite_note-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20) The new "Screen off memo" feature allows the phone to be awoken directly to a note screen when the stylus is removed,[[17]](#cite_note-techradar-5review-17) and the camera app allows public and private [livestreaming](/wiki/Livestreaming) directly to YouTube.[[17]](#cite_note-techradar-5review-17)

The Galaxy Note 7 was announced during a press event in New York City on 2 August 2016. It is largely based on the hardware of the [Galaxy S7](/wiki/Galaxy_S7), inheriting its processor, camera, and the restoration of [IP68](/wiki/IP68) water resistance and expandable storage, but with a larger 5.7-inch 1440p display. It is also Samsung's first device to feature a [USB-C](/wiki/USB-C) connector and the first water-protected device of the [Galaxy Note series](/wiki/Galaxy_Note_series), having a water-protected stylus too.

The Galaxy Note 7's display is curved across the sides of the device, and its stylus features higher degrees of pressure sensitivity (4096) and a finer tip.[[21]](#cite_note-verge-s7unveil-21)[[22]](#cite_note-ars-note7unveil-22) Samsung branded the device as the Note 7 rather than the Note 6 to synchronize its branding with the earlier flagship of the same year, the [Samsung Galaxy S7 series](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S7).[[23]](#cite_note-verge-gn7-23)

Upon release, the Galaxy Note series earned [criticism by a technology journalist of Android Police](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Note_7#Android_Police), criticizing that since 2015's Galaxy Note 5, not much except a stylus sets the Galaxy Note series flagship apart from the [Galaxy S series](/wiki/Galaxy_S_series) flagship released earlier in the same year, like it did with the first four generations of Galaxy Note devices.[[24]](#cite_note-AndroidPolice-24)

The Galaxy Note 7 was afflicted by repeated manufacturing problems with their internal batteries, which led to incidents in which they overheated and combusted.[[25]](#cite_note-verge-cause-25)[[26]](#cite_note-recode-cause-26) After replacement models experienced similar incidents, the Note 7 was officially discontinued on 11 October 2016, and nearly all units were recalled globally.[[27]](#cite_note-verge-note7isdead-27)[[28]](#cite_note-bbc-gn7done-28)

#### Galaxy Note Fan Edition
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=10)]

After the recall of the Samsung Galaxy Note 7, Samsung released the Note Fan Edition (FE) as a [refurbished](/wiki/Refurbishment_(electronics)) Note 7 in selected countries on 7 July 2017. Although having an identical form factor, the Fan Edition comes with a smaller battery of only 3200 mAh rather than the original Note 7 which is 3500 mAh due to safety reasons.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

Improved changes of the Galaxy Note Fan Edition include [Android Nougat](/wiki/Android_Nougat) with [Samsung Experience](/wiki/Samsung_Experience) 8.1 UI, [Bixby](/wiki/Bixby_(virtual_assistant)) virtual assistant (excluding Voice), a "Fan Edition" marking on the back and a Clear View Cover case.

The Samsung Galaxy Note 8 was announced on 23 August 2017. It features a 6.3" [1440p](/wiki/1440p) [Super AMOLED](/wiki/Super_AMOLED) Infinity Display, a 3300 mAh battery, Qualcomm [Quick Charge](/wiki/Quick_Charge) 2.0 support, [Snapdragon](/wiki/Qualcomm_Snapdragon) [835](/wiki/List_of_Snapdragon_devices#Snapdragon_835)/[Exynos](/wiki/Exynos) 8895 processor (depending on location), an [iris scanner](/wiki/Iris_scanner), IP68 dust and water resistance, a new dual-lens camera setup with a [telephoto lens](/wiki/Telephoto_lens) and support for [Samsung DeX](/wiki/Samsung_DeX).
[[30]](#cite_note-30)

On 27 June 2018, Samsung sent out invitations for the next "Unpacked" event, showing a yellow S Pen image. The Galaxy Note 9 was subsequently announced on 9 August 2018 and became available starting on 24 August 2018.[[31]](#cite_note-31)[[32]](#cite_note-32)

The Note 9 is a largely refined version of the Note 8. The biggest change from the Note 8 was the addition of [Bluetooth](/wiki/Bluetooth) functionality to the S-Pen, allowing a user to control the camera, YouTube videos and slideshows remotely.[[33]](#cite_note-33)

Internally, the Note 9 uses the [Snapdragon](/wiki/List_of_Qualcomm_Snapdragon_systems-on-chip) 845 or Exynos 9810 processor, with either 6 GB of RAM and 128 GB of internal storage, or 8 GB of RAM and 512 GB of internal storage, and a 4000 mAh battery.[[34]](#cite_note-34)

The Note 9 uses the same camera hardware seen on [Samsung Galaxy S9](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S9) Plus, with a dual camera setup, a 12MP wide-angle sensor with f/1.5 and f/2.4 dual aperture and a 12MP telephoto sensor with the f/2.4 aperture for [Bokeh](/wiki/Bokeh) effects at the back, along with an 8MP selfie camera.[[35]](#cite_note-35)

### Galaxy Note 10/Note 10+
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=13)]

On 1 July 2019, Samsung announced that it would hold its second Unpacked event of the year on 7 August at 16:00 Eastern in Brooklyn's Barclays Center. The Galaxy Note 10 and Note 10+ were unveiled at the show.[[36]](#cite_note-36)[[37]](#cite_note-37)

The Note 10 marked the first time Samsung offered a Plus model of its Note, with the Note 10 offering a 6.3-inch 1080p display Infinity-O Display and 3400 mAh battery, and the Note 10+ offering a 6.8-inch 1440p display with a 4300 mAh battery. The Note 10 has non-expandable 256 GB storage, while the Note 10+ has expandable 256/512 GB storage via microSD. Both phones added several new features from the [Samsung Galaxy S10](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S10), including in-display fingerprint scanners, Wireless Powershare (enabling the phone to be used to wirelessly charge other Qi-compatible devices), and triple camera arrays consisting of a 16MP ultra-wide angle lens and 12MP wide angle and telephoto lenses. Both variants also saw the power button consolidated with the Bixby button on the left side of the phone, with the button now being reprogrammable to be used as a power button or to activate Bixby, and eliminated the headphone jack.

Also introduced with the Note 10 variants were 25 watts Super Fast Charging (with the Note 10+ also being capable of 45 watt Super Fast Charging 2.0), marking the first charging rate increase since the 2014 Galaxy Note 4.[[38]](#cite_note-38)[[39]](#cite_note-verge-s10unveil-39)

#### Galaxy Note 10 Lite
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=14)]

On 3 January 2020, Samsung announced alongside the Galaxy S10 Lite, the upcoming release of the Note 10 Lite.[[40]](#cite_note-40) The Note 10 Lite's main points of interest were that it reintroduced design elements and features had not been used the flagship Note devices in a few generations, such as an entirely flat display (last seen on the Note 5), the reintroduction of the headphone jack (last seen on the Note 9), and the inclusion of an FM radio. Internally, the Note 10 Lite had the older chipset, processor, and GPU from the Exynos version of the Note 9, while incorporating newer features such as the triple cameras seen in the rest of the Note 10 series. To position itself, much as the Note 3 Neo had done, as a more affordable Note device, the pricing was much more comparable to midrange handsets of the time at under half the price of the Note 10+ and lesser than the Note 10. It had introduced the spen to the public at an affordable cost.

### Galaxy Note 20/Note 20 Ultra
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Samsung_Galaxy_Note&action=edit&section=15)]

Samsung announced the Galaxy Note 20 and Note 20 Ultra at a virtual Unpacked Event on 5 August 2020. Both came in variants with and without [5G](/wiki/5G) connectivity.

Like the Note 10 line, Note 20 has lesser specifications to justify a relatively lower price point, while the Note 20 Ultra is positioned as a high-end premium device. In this case, the Note 20 Ultra has a 6.9-inch display, 120 Hz refresh rate, 4,500 mAh battery, and expandable storage. The Note 20 lacks several key features of the Note 20 Ultra, including the high [refresh rate](/wiki/Refresh_rate), [microSD](/wiki/MicroSD) storage expansion and "periscope" [zoom lens](/wiki/Zoom_lens). Both phones have triple camera setups similar to the S20 line, with the Note 20 using two 12 MP wide and ultrawide sensors and a 64 MP telephoto sensor, and the Note 20 Ultra using a 108 MP wide sensor and two 12 MP telephoto and ultrawide sensors.[[41]](#cite_note-GSMArena-comparison-41) On both models, the buttons and S-Pen have switched places from their positions on the Note 10, with the power and volume buttons now being on the right side of the phone, and the S-Pen dock now moved to the left side of the USB-C port.

This is the last phone launched under the Note series, before Samsung decided to add support for S-Pen in the Galaxy S series and Z Fold series, beginning with the [Galaxy S21 Ultra](/wiki/Galaxy_S21_Ultra) and [Galaxy Z Fold 3](/wiki/Galaxy_Z_Fold_3). The [Galaxy S22 Ultra](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S22), launched in February 2022, features a built-in S-Pen.

The Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 is an 8-inch Android-based tablet computer produced and marketed by Samsung Electronics. It belongs to the second generation of the Samsung Galaxy Note series tablets, which also includes a 10.1-inch model, the Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition.

At the [Mobile World Congress](/wiki/Mobile_World_Congress) 2012, Samsung announced the Galaxy Note 10.1, as an alternative to the Galaxy Tab 10.1. It has a 10.1-inch display and uses a quad-core 1.4 GHz processor and supports the Samsung S-Pen stylus input as seen on the original Galaxy Note phone.

### Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition

At the 2013 Samsung Unpacked Episode 2 event in Berlin and New York, Samsung announced the successor to the original Galaxy Note 10.1-inch tablet dubbed as the Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition. Like its predecessor, it has a 10.1 inch display and now supports the improved Samsung S-Pen stylus input also seen in the Note III and it copies the design cue of its lower-end sibling the [Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Tab_3_10.1) which sports the unified Samsung design first used on the [Samsung Galaxy S4](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_S4).

### Galaxy Note Pro 12.2

At the 2014 Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Samsung announced the first Pro line of tablets which included a bigger Samsung Galaxy Note Pro tablet with a 12.2-inch display and also comes with the same S-Pen stylus the [Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Note_10.1_2014_Edition) is sporting which is the standard on the Note Series. Its design is similar to the [Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_Note_10.1_2014_Edition) which has the Samsung standard simulated stitched-leather back.

Subsequently, released together with the first regular Tab A 8.0 and 9.7 models in 2015, Samsung released a model of the Tab A 9.7 equipped with an S-Pen stylus making it the first Samsung Galaxy device to be equipped with the Samsung stylus outside the Note series. In 2017 Samsung released another S-Pen device, the Tab S3. On 1 August 2018, Samsung launched the new tablet: Samsung Galaxy Tab S4 with a new S-Pen. Subsequently, in 2019, Samsung launched the Galaxy Tab S6 with the S-Pen.

The Galaxy S21 Ultra was announced at the Galaxy Unpacked event on 14 January 2021, alongside the Galaxy S21 and Galaxy S21+. The Galaxy S21 Ultra is the first phone in the Galaxy S Series to support the S Pen accessory, albeit sold separately and with limited functionality. It features a 6.8" 1440p "Dynamic AMOLED" curved display with HDR10+ support, "dynamic tone mapping" technology, and a variable 120 Hz [refresh rate](/wiki/Refresh_rate).

The Galaxy S22 Ultra was announced at the Galaxy Unpacked event on 9 February 2022, alongside the Galaxy S22 and Galaxy S22+. Unlike the Galaxy S21 Ultra, the Galaxy S22 features an embedded S Pen, with similar functionalities to the Galaxy Note series and with a faster pen latency of 2.8ms.
